A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S-PUNA research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including the added Appendix I in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original S-PUNA experiments on ImageNet, TinyImageNet, and EuroSAT variants, including ablations, feature analyses, and cross-shift generalization results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds sensitivity experiments, downstream dataset-cleaning results, and an ACDC driving-condition evaluation.

M1.justification: The initialization, symmetric k-NN expansion, spectral-entropy stopping rule, and classifier distillation remain unchanged in Section 4. The additional layer, backbone, and application experiments reuse this procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix I adds normal-versus-adverse driving-condition detection on ACDC and a downstream TinyImageNet dataset-cleaning task assessed through classification accuracy. These extend the represented domain and task requirements beyond v1. The GenImage forgery discussion reuses existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their PU, supervised, OOD, and anomaly-detection methods. The new sensitivity table uses existing DCPU, DistPU, LaGAM, and SAPU baselines. The cleaning experiment adds clean/noisy training controls rather than a new competing detection algorithm.

E3.justification: v2 adds protocols with 5%, 25%, and 75% shifted samples and block-11 features alongside the retained balanced, block-6 experiments. Appendix I introduces two-epoch downstream classifier training on a 25% clean/75% corrupted mixture, evaluated by accuracy, and ACDC detection using unfine-tuned DINOv2 ViT-B/14 block-6 features. These are additional experimental designs, not revisions to the original benchmark settings.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds shifted-proportion sensitivity and an end-to-end block-11 comparison beyond v1's layerwise clustering analysis. Appendix C extends the epsilon, beta, k, and initialization-size ablations from ImageNet-R to ImageNet-V2. Together these substantially expand tests of imbalance, representation choice, and near-shift parameter sensitivity.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random seeds and retain mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for the main comparisons. Existing uncertainty values are unchanged, and v2 introduces no new statistical estimation procedure, significance test, or explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and transfer scores remain unchanged, but substantial results are added: Table 4 reports S-PUNA AUROC of 97.03 with block-11 features and 91.61 at 5% shifted samples; Appendix I reports 82.83 on ACDC and cleaning accuracy of 85.84%, versus 81.43% without cleaning. Table A.9 adds ImageNet-V2 sensitivity results. Appendix I.1 also reports 93.72% for ViT-based GenImage detection, although this matches the retained ResNet score and the ViT table reports 99.40%; that discrepancy does not establish a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: The PU-risk derivations, generalization bounds, Bayes-risk discussion, spectral-entropy lemma, and Appendix A proofs retain their mathematical content. Moving the pseudo-labeled dataset expression inline and renumbering subsequent equations do not change the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about PU-based covariate-shift detection, geometry-guided discovery, spectral stopping, competitive performance, and transferability. The added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 adds the interpretation that performance advantages are not merely a block-6 selection artifact and qualifies the classifier head's benefit as frequent rather than universal. Appendix I discusses practical utility for cleaning and deployment monitoring. Existing mechanism explanations and transfer limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address, HPC acknowledgments, and implementation information for the downstream experiments. Appendix B.4 newly states that EuroSAT-D was constructed independently of S-PUNA without tuning it to favor the method; this documents an existing construction rather than demonstrating a changed dataset procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a paragraph distinguishing shift detection from domain adaptation and generalization, using already cited literature. The references add the ACDC dataset paper. The remaining research positioning and cited works are retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 5.5 and Appendix I, expands related-work and ablation prose, and makes localized wording, author-affiliation, and running-header edits. The original narrative and section sequence largely remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 introduces Table 4 and expands v1's Table A.8 into Table A.9 with ImageNet-V2 columns. Existing figures retain their graphical content, while figure sizing, table placement, captions, and surrounding pagination receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added imbalance and layer-choice tests, near-shift ablations, and downstream experiments provide useful evidence beyond v1's evaluation, while the code-access statement improves reproducibility information. These support a modest net quality gain. The new GenImage passage introduces an unresolved backbone/score inconsistency, and the downstream experiments have limited protocol detail, tempering the benefit of the expanded evidence.
